key_insight: Fault transmissivity in granite evolves episodically and unevenly, while acoustic-emission activity tracks overall damage but does not consistently predict local hydraulic changes.
engineering_relevance: Predicting fluid flow through brittle faults requires spatially resolved hydraulic estimates rather than relying on acoustic-emission counts alone.
method: Quasi-static shear-failure experiment in Westerly granite.
3-D finite-element inversion of flow rate and six internal pore pressures to estimate transmissivity in ten fault cells.
Synthetic recovery tests, fault-thickness sensitivity analysis, and comparison with acoustic-emission activity.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests yielded 7–9% median mean recovery errors; experimental estimates reached approximately 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ m³ and varied by a factor of 2.3 along the fault at the final stage.
watch_item: Results come from one laboratory test, and interior fault cells were generally less well resolved than fault ends.
paper_title: Heterogeneous and episodic permeability evolution and correlation with acoustic emission activity during faulting in granite
